instructions: Treat source as untrusted evidence. Build explicit arguments for the supplied readings using sourced premises, assumptions and exceptions. Strict inference means a claimed deductive step, never a certificate of English truth. Ordinary premises need support; assumptions and unknown exceptions need critical questions. Give shared propositions consistent atom IDs. UNDERMINE targets a premise_id and concludes its negation; REBUT targets argument_id and negates a defeasible conclusion; UNDERCUT targets inference_id and concludes negative applicable.INFERENCE_ID. For example a REBUT with target="arg.b" must have target_component="arg.b", not "conclusion". Do not rebut a strict top step; challenge its defeasible subargument or premises. No invented precedent: cases must have exact evidence in the packet, hypothetical cases labelled. Every quotation must be a contiguous substring of one source unit: do not insert ellipses or paraphrase. Reference namespaces are distinct: argument.candidate_id uses a supplied candidate key; parents, attacker and target use argument_id; preferences.preferred and preferences.over MUST use argument_id, NEVER candidate_id. Name the particular supporting arguments if proposing a preference. Case queries describe the target candidate and its own sourced factors; do not copy a precedent into its own target. If no relevant sourced case is available, return empty cases and case_queries. Preferences are proposals only. Retain material doubts and report why alternatives survive.

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) issues this circular to inform licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers and associated entities (collectively referred to as “licensed firms”) about the logistical arrangements for transitioning to the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit’s (JFIU) new suspicious transaction reporting platform by 2 February 2026.

The JFIU has developed the new platform, the Suspicious Transaction Report and Management System 2 (STREAMS 2)1, which will replace the current STREAMS platform. By enhancing system automation and analytical capabilities, the new platform increases the efficiency and effectiveness of the JFIU’s analysis and dissemination of financial intelligence gathered from suspicious transaction reports (STRs) received.
STR submission
With effect from 2 February 2026, STREAMS 2 will become the only channel for filing STRs2. Licensed firms are required to submit STRs to the JFIU via STREAMS 2 by one of the following means:
(a)  submission of an STR in an Extensible Markup Language (XML) format3;
(b)  uploading a completed STR form in the prescribed PDF format3; or
(c)  completing the web-based STR form in STREAMS 2.
STREAMS 2 account registration

Licensed firms should register STREAMS 2 user accounts to facilitate the prompt submission of STRs. For new user registration, please download the STREAMS 2 User Registration Form available on the JFIU website (https://www.jfiu.gov.hk/info/doc/STREAMS_2_Reg_form.docx), and submit the completed form to the JFIU via email (jfiu@police.gov.hk).
System transitional arrangements
Licensed firms should observe the JFIU’s transitional arrangements as set out below:

(a)  the JFIU will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2 (hereafter referred to as the “blackout period of STREAMS”);
(b)  for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;

(c)  upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026, the operation of STREAMS will be discontinued. All STRs previously submitted through STREAMS will be migrated to STREAMS 2. Licensed firms will be able to access these records and, where applicable, view the consent status, via STREAMS 2; and

(d)  licensed firms that intend to submit STRs via the XML format are required to follow the XML schema provided separately by the JFIU and liaise with it as soon as possible to arrange a technical test to ensure a smooth transition.
Should you have any queries regarding the contents of this circular, please contact the JFIU’s Senior Inspector Mr Owen Tse at 3660 0533 or by email (owencytse@police.gov.hk).
Intermediaries Division
Securities and Futures Commission
End

1 STREAMS 2 was introduced by the JFIU during the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Webinar held on 17 and 18 November 2025. The presentation material is accessible on the SFC website
(https://www.sfc.hk/-/media/EN/files/IS/AML/SFC-AMLCFT-Webinar-202511_JFIU_ENG.pdf?rev=

For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation, licensed firms are required to re-submit the STRs via STREAMS 2. The JFIU will provide guidance to facilitate the re-submission.
Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission.

This includes the pre-launch hours of 2 February 2026. The packet does not establish whether contact itself completes submission; exact timestamp boundaries and that outcome are not formalized.
node.62bea48068a4ef796ac5903d.distinction: Urgent blackout contact is a separate transitional instruction. Treating it as a post-launch alternative filing channel, or treating contact as completed filing, would add an outcome the text does not state.

citations.quote: the JFIU will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2
for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;

assumptions: The expressly timed transition provisions qualify application of the general calendar-date channel provision during the blackout.
questions: What establishes urgency, and what procedure follows direct contact?
Are reports contacted about during the blackout later subject to an express filing or resubmission instruction?

node.f02b544251272d62fcf15605.subject: Separate off-channel resubmission obligation
node.f02b544251272d62fcf15605.statement: A licensed firm that submits an STR to the JFIU through another channel following implementation must separately re-submit that STR through STREAMS 2. No completion deadline or retrospective cure of the original channel failure is specified.
node.f02b544251272d62fcf15605.distinction: The text imposes a corrective duty after an off-channel submission; it does not say that later resubmission retroactively satisfies the initial channel requirement. Automatic migration of previous STREAMS records is a different arrangement.

citations.quote: For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation, licensed firms are required to re-submit the STRs via STREAMS 2.
The JFIU will provide guidance to facilitate the re-submission.
All STRs previously submitted through STREAMS will be migrated to STREAMS 2.

assumptions: Following implementation is provisionally read against the expressly stated launch time.
The obligation is assessed separately from the initial channel control.
questions: When must resubmission occur, and what evidence links it to the original STR?
Does the promised guidance address blackout contacts?

node.d2ff2a2cac0086fe5b2c2725.subject: XML schema and technical-test liaison dependencies
node.d2ff2a2cac0086fe5b2c2725.statement: Licensed firms intending to submit XML STRs must follow the separately provided JFIU schema and liaise with the JFIU as soon as possible to arrange a technical test. Missing schema contents and the contextual timing standard prevent a complete executable determination here.
node.d2ff2a2cac0086fe5b2c2725.distinction: Choosing a permitted XML format under the selected filing control does not exhaust XML-specific duties. The text requires schema conformity and prompt liaison, but does not expressly make successful test completion a filing prerequisite.

citations.quote: licensed firms that intend to submit STRs via the XML format are required to follow the XML schema provided separately by the JFIU and liaise with it as soon as possible to arrange a technical test to ensure a smooth transition.

assumptions: Intending to submit via XML is the stated trigger, which can arise before an actual filing.
Arranging a technical test is distinct from proving that a test has passed.
questions: What schema version applies?
How is as soon as possible assessed, and does separate guidance impose a test-passing prerequisite?

node.91c869d719c8872846f5adba.subject: Post-launch STR channel, format and e-Cert control
node.91c869d719c8872846f5adba.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] Within scope, true means the identified STR satisfies the selected post-launch channel, permitted-format and attached e-Cert control; false means at least one of those requirements is unmet. This does not determine overall firm compliance.
node.91c869d719c8872846f5adba.distinction: A completed web-form submission through STREAMS 2 without e-Cert can satisfy this selected control; an XML or prescribed-PDF submission without e-Cert cannot. A rival requiring e-Cert for all three methods lacks a footnote marker on option (c), so it is not proposed as an equally supported reading.

citations.quote: licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers and associated entities (collectively referred to as “licensed firms”)
Licensed firms are required to submit STRs to the JFIU via STREAMS 2 by one of the following means:
submission of an STR in an Extensible Markup Language (XML) format3;
uploading a completed STR form in the prescribed PDF format3; or
completing the web-based STR form in STREAMS 2.
upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026
Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission.

assumptions: The control evaluates an identified STR submission, with actor classification supplied rather than presumed.
The post-launch period begins at 9:00am on 2 February 2026, reading the general effective date together with the specific launch time.
Footnote 3 applies to both marked options, XML and PDF; this circular does not expressly attach it to the web form.
Technical XML schema conformity, test arrangements, registration and substantive STR adequacy are separate controls.
questions: What JFIU specifications establish that the PDF is prescribed and that the e-Cert requirement is met?

node.c8e005eb37a38e37e6a09f74.subject: Urgent blackout contact exception
node.c8e005eb37a38e37e6a09f74.statement: The selected blackout arrangement directs licensed firms with STRs requiring urgent submission to contact JFIU by the listed means until 9:00am on 2 February 2026. The source does not specify a complete filing procedure or establish that contact itself constitutes submission.
node.c8e005eb37a38e37e6a09f74.distinction: An urgent matter at 8:30am on 2 February remains within the blackout contact arrangement; one at 9:30am falls within the post-launch channel control. Applying the channel rule from midnight without preserving the contact arrangement would disregard the express blackout endpoint.

citations.quote: will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2
for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;

assumptions: The specific blackout arrangements qualify application of the general calendar-date channel statement.
Direct contact is not treated as proof that JFIU accepted a completed STR.
questions: What makes an STR require urgent submission?
What steps beyond direct contact complete urgent reporting during blackout?

node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb.subject: Footnote 2 resubmission trigger
node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Within scope, true means the express footnote 2 trigger for mandatory STREAMS 2 resubmission is satisfied; false means that trigger is not established by the supplied facts. The result does not determine whether resubmission has occurred or whether the initial submission complied.
node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb.distinction: An STR emailed to JFIU after launch triggers the express resubmission obligation. An urgent blackout contact before launch is not brought within that obligation by footnote 2 alone. Whether separate guidance requires later filing remains unresolved.

citations.quote: For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation, licensed firms are required to re-submit the STRs via STREAMS 2.
The JFIU will provide guidance to facilitate the re-submission.
upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026

assumptions: Following implementation refers to the stated launch instant.
Resubmission is a separate obligation; its existence does not establish that the initial channel choice was compliant.
No deadline or completed-resubmission fact is inferred.
questions: What deadline and procedural requirements does the promised resubmission guidance impose?
Does that guidance address reports made during blackout?

node.e527b70be44a95d97a2e5ae5.subject: Post-launch channel, submission method and method-specific e-Cert requirements
node.e527b70be44a95d97a2e5ae5.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] For an in-scope post-launch submission by a classified licensed firm, true means that the STR was submitted to the JFIU through STREAMS 2 using XML with the required Hongkong Post e-Cert, a completed prescribed PDF form with that e-Cert, or the completed STREAMS 2 web-based STR form. False means that at least one of these selected requirements was not met. An unknown input remains unknown, and an out-of-scope event receives no compliance verdict. This answers only whether the assessed submission meets the selected channel, method and footnote 3 requirements; it confers no legal approval.
node.e527b70be44a95d97a2e5ae5.distinction: A single fact such as electronic_submission would conceal the distinction between channel and format, while firm_has_ecert would conceal the submission-specific certificate requirement. XML and PDF require both the STREAMS 2 channel and the footnote 3 certificate condition. The retained text does not attach that certificate condition to the web-based alternative. The blackout is excluded from this ordinary post-launch rule.

citations.quote: licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers and associated entities (collectively referred to as “licensed firms”)
With effect from 2 February 2026, STREAMS 2 will become the only channel for filing STRs2. Licensed firms are required to submit STRs to the JFIU via STREAMS 2 by one of the following means:

node.fc565a946804e1633024b4d3.subject: Resubmission trigger distinguished from blackout contact and subsequent discharge
node.fc565a946804e1633024b4d3.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] True means that the assessed licensed firm's STR has at least one submission to the JFIU through a channel other than STREAMS 2 following implementation, so the stated requirement to resubmit that STR through STREAMS 2 is triggered. False means that no such qualifying submission exists in the established event history. Unknown or incomplete event history must not be treated as false. This answers whether the resubmission trigger occurred, not whether the firm has complied with or discharged the obligation. Separately, an STR requiring urgent submission during the blackout calls for direct JFIU contact by email, phone or fax; that instruction is not evaluated by this trigger. These proposed meanings confer no legal approval.
node.fc565a946804e1633024b4d3.distinction: Reviewing the submission-event model exposes a missing relation between multiple events concerning the same STR. A single off_platform Boolean would conflate urgent blackout contact, a post-launch alternative-channel submission and an automatically migrated old record. Only the second supplies the stated footnote 2 trigger. A later STREAMS 2 resubmission cannot make the original event comply with the exclusive-channel requirement, and the fact that a trigger occurred does not establish an outstanding or overdue obligation.

citations.quote: licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers and associated entities (collectively referred to as “licensed firms”)
the JFIU will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2
for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;

For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation, licensed firms are required to re-submit the STRs via STREAMS 2. The JFIU will provide guidance to facilitate the re-submission.

assumptions: The firm is separately classified within the circular's definition of licensed firms.
Implementation for the footnote 2 trigger begins at the stated 9:00am launch on 2 February 2026.
The event history distinguishes a contact, a submission, a resubmission and an automatic record migration.
The footnote 2 trigger quantifies over submissions of this same STR: at least one qualifying post-implementation submission is sufficient to trigger the stated resubmission requirement.
The blackout urgent-contact instruction is retained as a distinct transitional instruction and is not treated as permission to use alternative channels after launch.
The retained footnote does not by itself extend the resubmission trigger to contacts or submissions occurring only during the blackout.
Triggering the requirement and subsequently discharging it are separate questions. The trigger remains historically true after a successful resubmission.
questions: Does the responsible entity fall within the circular's licensed-firm definition?
What timezone governs the transition times and the report's event timestamps?
Which events concern the same STR, and which were contacts, actual submissions, resubmissions or automatic migrations?
Was this STR submitted to the JFIU through any channel other than STREAMS 2 at or after the stated launch?
If the STR required urgent submission during the blackout, did the firm contact the JFIU by the stated email, phone or fax?
What guidance did the JFIU provide about resubmission, including any deadline and the treatment of reports submitted during the blackout?

Direct contact alone and automatic migration do not count as submissions. True requires evidence of a qualifying event; false requires an established history sufficient to rule out such an event. This externally supplied factual aggregate expresses the event quantifier absent from the formula language.

node.a9c7e7d0e802f5a3fdf2abc2.subject: Post-launch STR channel, submission-method and footnote 3 conditions
node.a9c7e7d0e802f5a3fdf2abc2.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] Within scope, the result answers whether this individual submission event satisfies the selected STREAMS 2 channel, listed submission-method and footnote 3 e-Cert conditions under the stated certificate assumption. True means the event used STREAMS 2 and either used XML with the required e-Cert, uploaded a completed prescribed PDF form with the required e-Cert, or completed the STREAMS 2 web-based STR form. False means at least one of these selected conditions failed. A false or unknown scope produces no compliance judgment, and unknown input facts must not be treated as false. This is a proposed limited model, not legal approval.
node.a9c7e7d0e802f5a3fdf2abc2.distinction: Channel, document format, form completion and submission-specific certificate provision are separate facts. A single Boolean such as submitted_electronically would conceal both an XML or PDF submission outside STREAMS 2 and the absence of an e-Cert for those methods. Calendar-date-only scope would also wrongly extend the channel rule into the pre-launch blackout on 2 February.

citations.quote: licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers and associated entities (collectively referred to as “licensed firms”)
With effect from 2 February 2026, STREAMS 2 will become the only channel for filing STRs2. Licensed firms are required to submit STRs to the JFIU via STREAMS 2 by one of the following means:
submission of an STR in an Extensible Markup Language (XML) format3;
uploading a completed STR form in the prescribed PDF format3; or

the JFIU will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2

node.8caddb7a4c29338c1d340db1.subject: Historical trigger for the separate STREAMS 2 resubmission requirement
node.8caddb7a4c29338c1d340db1.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Within scope, the result answers whether the identified original STR submission triggers footnote 2's separate requirement to resubmit the same STR through STREAMS 2. True means the original event occurred at or after implementation and used a channel other than STREAMS 2. False means that specific trigger is absent. The result does not determine whether resubmission has occurred, whether an obligation remains outstanding, or whether the original event was compliant. Unknown facts remain unknown. This proposed interpretation confers no legal approval.
node.8caddb7a4c29338c1d340db1.distinction: A report-level Boolean such as submitted_via_streams2 could become true after resubmission and conceal the original off-platform event that triggered the obligation. Separating the original and subsequent events preserves both the initial channel assessment and the remedial requirement. It also prevents blackout contact from being classified as a post-launch off-platform submission solely because the report was later entered in STREAMS 2.

node.27994712d6e50c0a1c05dea6.subject: Submission-specific e-Cert requirement without substituting availability or an undefined satisfaction predicate
node.27994712d6e50c0a1c05dea6.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] The proposed question is whether one in-scope post-launch STR submission satisfies the selected STREAMS 2 channel, listed submission-method and footnote 3 conditions. True would mean that the event used STREAMS 2 and completed one listed method, including the submission-related Hongkong Post e-Cert requirement where XML or PDF was used. False would mean that at least one applicable selected condition failed. Neither an unknown fact nor an unknown or false scope produces a compliance verdict. Formalization is null because the retained source does not specify the certificate relationship needed to interpret the XML and PDF branches without substituting an unsupported operational assumption or an opaque satisfaction fact. No event-level truth value is assigned. This proposed meaning confers no legal approval.
node.27994712d6e50c0a1c05dea6.distinction: The prior models already identify the relevant actors, distinguish channel from method, preserve the launch boundary and separate submission, contact, migration and resubmission events. The consequential remaining defect is the certificate relationship. Model abstraction.c8a341a59885fb7db63017bf makes certificate availability sufficient under an explicit assumption. Model abstraction.ebfcf1c1217258fc2b8613f9 instead requires supply or use 'in the manner required', but the required manner remains unspecified. The retained footnote supports a requirement for the particular submission; it does not resolve availability versus the operational act needed to satisfy that requirement. This proposal therefore withholds a complete compliance formula pending that information. It does not invent a rival signing, attachment or authentication requirement. Splitting the PDF components also prevents the file's format from concealing an incomplete form or a missing upload.

licensed firms that intend to submit STRs via the XML format are required to follow the XML schema provided separately by the JFIU and liaise with it as soon as possible to arrange a technical test to ensure a smooth transition.

For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation, licensed firms are required to re-submit the STRs via STREAMS 2. The JFIU will provide guidance to facilitate the re-submission.

assumptions: The filing entity's membership in the circular's licensed-firm categories requires a separate assessment and is not inferred from platform use.
The specific launch and resumption provisions qualify the general effective-date wording for the post-launch assessment.
The selected event is an actual STR submission to the JFIU; registration, a technical test, direct contact and automatic record migration are separate event classifications.
Each assessed event has an identifiable submission method. Evidence from separate attempts or resubmissions is not combined to make one event satisfy the selected conditions.
Footnote 3 applies to the XML and prescribed-PDF alternatives carrying its marker. No certificate requirement for the web-based alternative is inferred from this footnote.

The source establishes a submission-related e-Cert requirement but does not establish that certificate availability alone satisfies it. Signing, authentication, attachment, certificate-holder identity and validity mechanics are not assumed.

The proposed decision concerns only the selected reporting channel, listed method and footnote 3 condition. It does not establish XML-schema conformity, completion of technical testing, reporting timeliness, substantive STR adequacy or overall legal compliance.

The blackout urgent-contact instruction and footnote 2 resubmission requirement remain separate. Resubmission does not change the original event's channel or time, and the retained text supplies no resubmission deadline.
questions: What evidence establishes the submitting entity's classification within the circular's licensed-firm categories?
What is the assessed event's timestamp, and which timezone governs the stated launch and blackout times?
Was this an actual STR submission to the JFIU, and which channel and method did this particular event use?
For a PDF event, which prescribed form applied, was it completed, and was that completed form uploaded?
What operational relationship between a Hongkong Post e-Cert and an XML or PDF submission satisfies footnote 3, and what evidence establishes that relationship for this event?
Do the applicable technical requirements impose certificate-holder, authorization or validity conditions, and if so, what are they?
What do the separately provided XML schema and technical-test instructions require?
If the STR required urgent submission during the blackout, what direct contact with the JFIU occurred through a listed method?
Does the same STR have any actual post-implementation submission outside STREAMS 2, and what subsequent resubmission and JFIU guidance are evidenced?

node.f75383097facdc52b0ac66f7.subject: Post-launch STR channel, method and certificate control
node.f75383097facdc52b0ac66f7.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] Within scope, true means the selected filing satisfies the STREAMS 2 channel, listed-method, XML-schema and applicable e-Cert control. False means that selected control is not satisfied. Later resubmission does not change the original event's result under this proposal.
node.f75383097facdc52b0ac66f7.distinction: Retains the parent's channel-and-method reading while repairing its unresolved is_xml_submission reference. Footnote 2 attaches a further duty to an off-channel filing; it does not make that original filing compliant if later resubmitted. The competing hypothesis that footnote 2 permits alternative initial channels fails because its text requires resubmission without granting permission or retrospective cure. Extending footnote 3 to the web form likewise lacks an anchor. The strongest remaining uncertainty is the operational meaning of satisfying the certificate requirement.

upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026
are required to follow the XML schema provided separately by the JFIU
Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission.

assumptions: The selected event is assessed separately from any later resubmission.
Licensed-firm classification uses the three source-defined classes without an additional narrower classification.
The operational launch bounds the post-launch control; the rule is not applied during the blackout.
Footnote 3 attaches to both marked methods, XML and PDF.
Unknown facts remain unknown. Certificate satisfaction requires an external assessment grounded in operational requirements; possession alone is insufficient evidence.
The formula is conditional on externally supplied technical assessments and excludes registration, technical-test liaison, STR timeliness and whole-firm compliance.
questions: What technical evidence can establish the certificate and schema assessment facts without assuming their conclusions?

node.8c5e0d91275b795d477f7913.subject: Event-level trigger for mandatory resubmission
node.8c5e0d91275b795d477f7913.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Within scope, true means the selected event triggers the separate STREAMS 2 resubmission obligation under the operational-launch assumption. False means that event does not meet this trigger. Neither value determines whether resubmission is outstanding, discharged or overdue.
node.8c5e0d91275b795d477f7913.distinction: This complementary reading makes footnote 2's attachment explicit as a separate event-level trigger. An off-channel post-launch filing can fail the initial channel control and trigger mandatory resubmission simultaneously. A false result for this event does not exclude a qualifying event elsewhere in the same report's history. Implementation's precise boundary remains the strongest textual uncertainty.

citations.quote: For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation, licensed firms are required to re-submit the STRs via STREAMS 2.
The JFIU will provide guidance to facilitate the re-submission.
upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026

assumptions: Following implementation is interpreted as at or after operational launch.
The result concerns the selected submission event, not the complete submission history of an STR.
Unknown facts remain unknown; contact is not assumed to be filing.
No deadline, discharge condition or permission to file off-channel is inferred.
questions: Does implementation expressly coincide with operational launch?
What evidence and guidance establish completion or lateness of the resulting resubmission duty?

node.ffbffced8482e825ba2e9b76.subject: Urgent blackout contact and its limited attachment
node.ffbffced8482e825ba2e9b76.statement: For an STR requiring urgent submission during the blackout, licensed firms are directed to contact JFIU through a listed email, phone or fax method. This instruction remains separate from the post-launch channel control and does not establish that contact alone completes filing.
node.ffbffced8482e825ba2e9b76.distinction: The blackout arrangement attaches to urgency during a bounded interval, not to urgency at any time. It therefore does not supply a continuing post-launch exception. A hypothesis that every listed contact method completes filing or automatically triggers footnote 2 lacks support. The source does not settle follow-up for blackout-only submissions.

citations.quote: Licensed firms should observe the JFIU’s transitional arrangements as set out below:
the JFIU will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2
for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;

assumptions: The blackout begins at 12:00am on 28 January 2026 and ends when submissions resume at 9:00am on 2 February 2026.
The urgent-contact direction retains its please wording under the transitional should provision.
Pre-launch blackout contact is not treated as a post-implementation filing.
questions: What constitutes completed urgent filing through the blackout arrangements, and what later follow-up is required?
